findings.evidence: Rubric: "we can avoid making lemmas rely on defeq downstream by using := (rfl) instead of := rfl." All four bodies are literally `rfl` (L62, L215, L233, L238).
findings.fix: Use `:= (rfl)` on these four lemmas so consumers rewrite through the stated API rather than relying on definitional unfolding.
findings.issue: The characteristic lemmas proved by `rfl` (`induced_coact` L215, `subtypeLinear_apply` L62, `subtype_toLinearMap` L233, `subtype_apply` L238) are `:= rfl`, so downstream proofs can close these goals by defeq and bypass the named lemmas.

findings.evidence: L57 `@[expose] def subtypeLinear`, L224 `@[expose] noncomputable def subtype`; L64-66 uses `Subtype.val_injective` against `⇑N.subtypeLinear`; L22-26 `## Main declarations` lists only `inducedCoact`, `instComodule`, `subtype`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[expose]` on both. If later kernel/finite-dimensional work needs injectivity of the inclusion (as the docstring anticipates), add `subtype_injective`/`subtypeLinear_injective` as lemmas instead of exposing the body to recover `Subtype.val_injective` by defeq.
findings.issue: `subtypeLinear` (L57) and `subtype` (L224) are `@[expose]`, but no consumer in this PR must unfold or compute them; `subtypeLinear_apply`, `subtype_apply`, and `subtype_toLinearMap` already characterize them. `subtypeLinear` is not even listed in `## Main declarations`. The only defeq the exposed body enables downstream is `⇑subtypeLinear = Subtype.val` (for injectivity).

summary: Characteristic API is complete and correctly annotated, but the rfl-proven characteristic lemmas use bare `:= rfl` and two definitional wrappers are `@[expose]` with no consumer needing their bodies; both let downstream bypass the stated interface via defeq.
